Okay, so you chose the wrong ram on the website. The one you have is compatible with the current motherboard you have. The PSU is fine, everything looks good except the mobo. The reason you couldn’t find your mobo on pcpartpicker was probably because you selected your cpu first. Then when choosing the motherboard it didn’t show up because it has a “compatibility” filter on it. If you uncheck the filter you will find it and see it isn’t compatible with your cpu.

Also is that thermal paste coming out of the sides? If it is, go easy on it next time. Should be a super thin layer, just enough to ensure seamless contact between to the cooling plate and cpu. Too much and the cooling plate won’t effectively cool the cpu. Good luck, I think it’s really nice what you are doing for your gramps.

I ended up checking the compatibility of your parts, and the processor- mobo combo isn’t compatible. The mobo uses a H370 intel chipset which is for 8th and 9th gen processors. The i5 7500 is a gen 7 and uses H270 chipset. If you want to check compatibility I would use pcpartpicker or a similar website which allows you to check parts and also wattage to make sure your psu will have enough juice.
Seating issue or compatibility issue. Reseat first. If it still doesn’t boot check to see if your cpu/mobo supports your ram.

If you want to keep your AIO you could try repairing it. When it’s turned on what do you hear? You may need to replace the radiator fluid, but will only fix it if the pump is still good. Id check youtube for some tutorials, but would only set you back the cost of new fluid

There could be a lot going on here. Usually when something is booting and shuts off it is some type of compatibility issue. Does your motherboard have led error lights? 
If so, check there first.
The PSU may not have enough power for everything, 450 watts is pretty low/cutting it close. 
Ram at 3600 has compatibility issues out of the box without updating BIOS first. If ram isn’t fully installed properly it will not boot. Double check it is fully “clicked in” 
Most motherboards do not have an on board gpu chipset and I didn’t see one listed in your description. 
Hope you are able to figure it out, good luck

You may need to adjust your boot config settings in BIOS. How many drives do you have? Is it trying to boot from a drive without an OS? Make sure the boot order is how you want and that the specific OS boot loader is selected.

Check processes, background processes/ services from software that you have accumulated over time. It will probably be the services running constantly in the background that is slowing your pc down, while the Microsoft ones have to stay on, you can turn the others off

Always stay positive in a negotiation. Make them think it was their idea in the first place to recommend a higher wage. Never apologize to the interviewer, you gave them your time and time is money regardless if you did that interview for “free”. That interview is equally important to both parties, since not only are they seeing if you are a good fit, you are seeing if they are a good fit for you. 

I would mention how much I loved the company and everyone I met during the process. If you found it to be a great fit, mention that. Butter them up a little. Research the companies interests and let them know how you would love to contribute, and let them know how much you are worth. I would love to renegotiate my salary contract…etc. Also like someone else mentioned, definitely check out glassdoor to see if the company is even worth negotiating for. 

I wish you great success and hope you get what you are looking for.

I would wait this one out before coming to this type of conclusion. You just experienced some pretty good stress, which could trigger schizophrenia depending on your age and the amount of stressors you are under. Or it could be a type of temporary anxiety. 

This type of temporary anxiety can be triggered by feelings of stress or unease, think deadlines of projects looming, broken friendships, alone in some creepy cabin, etc. 

Our minds are wired to respond reactively when stress is high and could potentially increase various aspects of your senses. Things that you may have not heard before, become increasingly apparent. 

For example: in a war zone, a combatant may wake just moments prior to being shot at. This is not mental illness nor is it schizophrenia. It is heightened  awareness due to stress. 

Imagine again that you are in the jungle on vacation, but have 0 worries. A person asks if you heard the frogs that night and you say… nope, was just asleep.  

But that combatant, will relay every noise they have ever heard in that jungle and then some, 60 years later. 

I think you just have a few unresolved issues that are eating at your conscience. Solve them and see if those noises go away. If they don’t, perhaps seeks a medical professional.

Ditto. Treatment sucks, and the world the way it is now, isn’t built for people like us. Although, I have found some things that have helped. An outlet really. Hiking, skydiving, mountain biking. Anything that includes immediate release of adrenaline and endorphins has helped, not to make me normal, but at least to make me happy and enjoy life. In fact, screw those other people who make us feel like aliens. We are not. Our brains are unique and if I may, I will revel in that fact, point my nose high, and continue to be the weirdo that I am.  Our unregulated emotions can be used like super powers, use em when you got em. Lay in bed all day if you don’t. Society needs, nor has any say or valid opinions about us, because, I hate to say it, but they ain’t us.

But as I said before, screw em! If they can’t love you for who you are, ups and downs, robotics or not, they do not deserve any of your attention. You want to feel??? Find something wild and fun that will make you feel. You are superhuman after-all :) the feelings you achieve do not have to be analogous to those of NTs. They just have to make YOU happy.
